phase_9_audit.question: Does the current unified selector (perf_model/cost_model_registry.py CostEstimate, perf_model/matmul_bias_relu_cost_model.py MatMulBiasReLUCostModel) support p95 latency, median latency, stability ratio, performance gate, or policy rejection reason?
phase_9_audit.finding: NO. CostEstimate (perf_model/cost_model_registry.py) has fields: candidate_id, predicted_latency_ms, source, confidence, is_extrapolation, evidence_note. It has no p95/stability/performance-gate/rejection-reason field. MatMulBiasReLUCostModel.predict() returns only the raw measured median latency. The ONLY place a p95/median stability gate exists in the whole repository is the pre-existing, separate deployment.execution_plan.slice3c_target_selection.validate_measurement() function (max_p95_over_median<=1.25), which the unified selector does not call.
phase_9_audit.classification: SOURCE_PROVEN (read cost_model_registry.py, matmul_bias_relu_cost_model.py, slice3c_target_selection.py in full)

path_b_rationale: Path A (minimal integration) would require: (1) adding new optional fields to CostEstimate (generic core file, already proven byte-identical-except-for-E2E-10's-necessary-fix across two slices -- a third edit is not 'minimal' relative to the goal of leaving it alone), (2) populating those fields for MatMul specifically while leaving RMSNorm/LM-head's cost models untouched (fine), (3) inserting a NEW step in the generic selection ORDER inside select_implementation() or a wrapper around it (kernel legality -> accuracy gate -> performance/stability gate -> cost comparison -> fallback) -- this is a five-stage pipeline change to the one file (implementation_decision.py) that has remained byte-identical since E2E-9, which is the single most load-bearing 'strongest claim' artifact validated across E2E-9, E2E-10, and E2E-11 Phase 0.

Given the explicit instruction to prefer no code changes this slice and to choose Path B when Path A would require more than minimal, narrowly-scoped work, and given this same trade-off was already flagged as a known, explained gap at the end of E2E-10, Path B (run the original production selector beside the unified selector, report the mismatch explicitly, classify fidelity as PARTIAL) is chosen for E2E-11 as well.

production_vs_unified_agreement.explanation_of_the_difference_between_ru: Real, reproducible, run-to-run measurement variance at microsecond-scale latencies. At 1x1x1 and 2x2x2, all 3 INT8 candidates' p95/median ratio hovers right around the 1.25 stability-gate threshold (measured 1.01-1.51 across the two runs) -- small OS/process-scheduling jitter at this scale can push a candidate's ratio to either side of 1.25, flipping whether the production selector's stability gate accepts or rejects it. This is not selector misbehavior; it IS what the stability gate is designed to guard against (untrustworthy latency at ultra-tiny operation sizes), and the unified selector's absence of this gate is precisely why it disagrees at exactly these boundary shapes and nowhere else.
production_vs_unified_agreement.classification: unified MatMul selector fidelity to the gated production policy: PARTIAL (not 9/9). Explicitly NOT claimed as 9/9.
